newsitem.title: USA: Brent, intermonth spreads up in U.S. paper trading.
newsitem.headline: Brent, intermonth spreads up in U.S. paper trading.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude and intermonth spreads were stronger in late U.S. paper trading on Friday, traders said.
A full boat of July Brent traded at $18.85 a barrel, up 10 cents from the settlement of London's IPE.
Two partials traded at $18.80 and $18.77 a barrel, confirming the uptick.
Intermonth spreads reinforced the market's newfound backwardation, in which prompt prices exceed forward ones.
June/July Brent changed hands at plus eight cents, up from plus three cents earlier in the day.
July/August Brent traded once at flat and twice at plus two cents, up from talk of minus three cents to minus one cent earlier.
Finally, August/September was dealt at minus one cent, extending the upward curve, traders said.
